rationale: Both candidates cover the two substantive ground-truth points (regression tests added, CuMemTag enum added per Gaohan123's request) with grounded, actionable findings. Y is the only one to hit the latent gap: it explicitly flags that the blanket NotImplementedError on level-2 wake will break five existing hardware-gated tests that sleep(level=2) then wake_up(), and notes diffusion workers actually implement level-2 restore via buffer copy-back — this precisely anticipates the real #4905/#4912 incident. X's related finding (default level=2 bricking the engine) is valid but addresses a different mechanism and never questions existing test/CI compatibility. Y's report is denser and has some redundancy (the level-2 blocker is stated twice near-verbatim), slightly hurting precision, but its concurrency race-condition finding and tag-validation finding are additional well-grounded, actionable issues X misses.
